standard_prerequisites: The projective bundle formula, describing the Chow groups of a projective space bundle as a free module over those of the base, and the computation of the pushforward of powers of the first Chern class of the tautological quotient
The notion of a bivariant class, and the closure of bivariance under capping with a first Chern class, under flat pullback and under proper pushforward
The Segre class construction assigning to every base change of the projective bundle a map by pushing forward a power of the Chern class capped with the pullback
core_obligations: Deduce uniqueness of the maps c_i from the projective bundle formula together with the normalisation c_0 equal to the identity

Observe that the Segre class maps, defined by pushing forward a suitable power of the first Chern class of the tautological quotient capped with the pullback, are bivariant classes by the closure properties
Use the projective bundle computations to see that the Segre classes vanish in negative degree and that the zeroth one is the identity
Push the relation displayed in the statement forward to the base and read off the first Chern class as the first Segre class, hence as a bivariant class

Repeat the procedure after multiplying the relation by the first Chern class of the tautological quotient and pushing forward, obtaining the second Chern class in terms of Segre classes, and continue inductively to conclude that every c_i is bivariant
proof_roadmap: Get uniqueness from the projective bundle formula and the normalisation
Build the Segre classes and check they are bivariant with the expected vanishing and normalisation
Push the defining relation forward iteratively to exhibit each Chern class as a bivariant class
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the existence and uniqueness of the Chern classes as bivariant classes characterised by the projective bundle relation at source lines 4596-4618, label lemma-segre-classes, whose proof occupies source lines 4620-4654. Uniqueness is immediate from the projective bundle formula together with the normalisation c_0 equal to the identity, but existence requires the Segre class construction: the proof defines maps by pushing forward a power of the first Chern class of the tautological quotient capped with the pullback, verifies through the closure properties of bivariant classes that these are bivariant, records their vanishing in negative degree and their normalisation from the projective bundle computations, and then runs an induction in which the defining relation is multiplied by the first Chern class and pushed forward to express c_1, then c_2, and so on, as bivariant classes. The counted statement records neither the induction nor the Segre class construction.
